body:
I'm just guessing here, but I don't think it's necessary to mention the `_on_ready` part since it'll most likely be understood that it comes before processing, so that's the best place to do it. Idk the common usecases for using notifications that already have methods like these directly, but I'd say that the users who use them understand Godot well. Maybe it can be shortened down to this:
```suggestion
			[b]Note:[/b] Using this notification does not enable physics processing automatically.
```
That said, I'm still not sure if it's needed since the link to `_physics_process` is there, but I guess it's not that obvious to assume from its description that it's the only special case that turns it on, I'd say. Most new users would think processing for nodes is always on by default.

Also do the same for `NOTIFICATION_PROCESS` if you decide to take my suggestion.

+			[b]Note:[/b] using this notification in [method Object._notification] doesn't automatically call [code]set_physics_process(true)[/code]. You must call it yourself on [method _ready].
body:
Sorry for my persistence, but I do _personally_ think this note is not strictly necessary. Not only that, but seeing it in practice I think it's misleading. It leads the reader come to the wrong conclusions, it portrays Godot's inner workings wrong.

"What do you mean it does not enable something? Can other notifications know when they're accessed? Can all constants do that?"
But constants are just values, they can't do anything on their own. Godot (& GDScript) barely do any "magic", and I wouldn't personally want users to start making assumptions like these.

(Also the note should be added to the other notifications with corresponding setters)
